name: addpipe24_carry_select_1212
rationale: All previously tried block-partition masks (e.g. 12+12, 8+8+8) split the addition into serially chained sub-adds (carry rippling from low block into high block), which strictly lengthens the critical path versus the monolithic '+' and empirically hurt WNS (7.38 vs 7.52). A true carry-select adder instead precomputes the upper 12-bit sum twice in parallel (assuming cin=0 and cin=1, using the same efficient tool-inferred '+' adder synthesis that produces the best-known baseline), and only adds a single final 2:1 mux stage selecting based on the actual carry out of the lower 12-bit block. This removes the serial dependency that hurt the naive splits: critical path becomes max(low-block delay, up-block delay) + one mux level, instead of low-block + up-block in series. Since the tool's own '+' synthesis for a 24-bit operand already achieves near log-depth timing (matching our best hand-built prefix adder), a 12-bit sub-add is only marginally shallower, but removing the serial carry dependency previously measured to cost ~0.14ns of WNS is a plausible lever to recover or exceed baseline WNS while area grows only modestly from the extra redundant 12-bit adder and mux.
